title: A sparse matrix with an indexer
description:
Write `public class SparseMatrix` that stores only the cells that are not zero, in a `Dictionary<(int Row, int Col), double>`:

- `new SparseMatrix(rows, cols)`; both must be positive (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`).
- `Rows`, `Cols`, and `NonZero` (how many cells are stored).
- An indexer `this[int row, int col]`: reading an unset cell gives 0; setting 0 removes the cell; a position outside the matrix throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- `operator +` for two matrices of the same size (otherwise `ArgumentException`), and `operator *` for a matrix times a `double`.
- `ToString()` with one line per row, values separated by single spaces, using the default `double` formatting (`"0 1.5 0"`), lines joined with `"\n"`.
hints: The indexer's setter is where "zero means absent" lives: `if (value == 0) _cells.Remove(key); else _cells[key] = value;`. Then `result[r, c] += v` in `+` cleans up cells that cancel out by itself.
A tuple key `(row, col)` works in a dictionary because tuples compare by value. `foreach (var ((r, c), v) in _cells)` takes each entry apart in one line.
